posts.author: Solar_Flare
posts.body: Cross-origin is definitely something that breaks RPGMaker games quite frequently. For example, if you upload it to Itch.io, it'll be shown in a frame, and usually fail to load because the frame is on a different domain than Itch.io. In that case you can right-click and choose "Show only this frame", and it'll work. I'd suggest trying that on your uploaded game, at least as a test to see if it's the problem.

posts.author: DevRPG2k
posts.body:
Something I had no trouble with, right-clicking, worked normally:
But I didn't even need to; I opened it with F12 by clicking on the address bar to avoid freezing and found the problem:
When uploading the files, specifically this "iphone-inline-video.browser.js" file is deleted, likely for violating some usage rule.
How to fix:
In index.html, remove line 19:
<script type="text/javascript" src="js/libs/iphone-inline-video.browser.js"></script>
In rpg_core.js, remove line 2505:
makeVideoPlayableInline(this._video);
Working:
Don't get me wrong, but let's say hypothetically you don't know how to open Notepad and locate a line using
Edit
-->
Go to Line...
(Ctrl + G)... install this plugin that's attached
Edit:
Another tip, I might be wrong, but in my tests none of my laptops required m4a, so web players probably won't need this format. As you can see in all the audio folders, each song has two formats; if you remove all m4a files, the size of your project will be drastically reduced.

My mistake, I understood that few files were being played, not the opposite.
Given this, the only way to determine the cause is through DEBUG.
Install this plugin, then use the debugger to enable the switch you defined to force the M4A format, or disable it to force OGG (fixed):
JavaScript:
AudioManager.audioFileExt = function() {
    return ($gameSwitches._data[1])? '.m4a' : '.ogg';
};
This is just for testing purposes.
If it doesn't work, as I said before, you'll need to reconvert these files using FFMPEG preferably. Search Google for the command lines with the correct codecs for these formats.
